answer: In this PoA scheme, each identity must complete a prescribed chain of modular squarings, where every result depends on the previous one; GPUs cannot parallelize that chain to remove its sequential delay. An attacker can run separate chains for multiple clones in parallel, but each still incurs the full time-lock cost, making mass identities costly rather than physically impossible. Wesolowski proofs let nodes verify completion efficiently, whether the computation marks a voyage, a summit, or a zephyr.
